sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chartering and Operation of Offshore Platform Support Ships

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement (1989, as amended)
Luxembourg–Belgium Double Taxation Agreement (1970, as amended)
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Convention (1996, as amended by 2004 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme); CSSF Regulation 12-02; Law of 27 July 2018 establishing the central Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2018; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Societies, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Corporate Registration Extract of each corporate shareholder or general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies/Commercial Registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) if origin country is a Contracting State; otherwise consular legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Attestation de bonne fin of each corporate shareholder and proposed general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade registry, tax administration, or competent corporate registrar in the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn French/Luxembourgish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner declaration, organizational chart, and UBO register extract disclosing natural persons owning 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each corporate shareholder/general partner, verified and notarized by a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized deed or certified copy with Hague Apostille / consular legalization of the underlying corporate records

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport/national ID copies and proof of residential address of each natural-person UBO and of the general partner(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/ID issuing state authority, bank/utility provider for proof of address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies before a Luxembourg notary or sworn legalization by the issuing Embassy; where possible, apostille for public documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg notary and incorporation agent to file and sign the SCSp incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostillized/consularly legalized in the grantor's state of residence, with sworn translation if not in French/German/Luxembourgish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, general partners, natural-person beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions, OFAC SDN list (where relevant for USD clearing), FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions, and domestic Luxembourg sanctions registers. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and their family members/close associates receive enhanced due diligence under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. Any hit requires immediate escalation to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal: lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Latin characters. French, German, Luxembourgish, or any EU-language Latin-script name is accepted; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin script and rendered in a form recognizable under Luxembourg naming law. The legal form suffix 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or 'SCSp' must appear. Names must not mislead the public as to legal form, public authority status, or regulated activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank – prior CSSF authorization required
Assurance / Réassurance – prior Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) authorization required
Fonds d'investissement / OPCVM / SICAV – prior CSSF authorization required
Fiduciaire / Trust – ministerial or professional-body approval required
État / Gouvernement / National / Commune – prior ministerial authorization required to avoid misleading official-status implication
Luxembourg / Ville de Luxembourg – prior state or municipal approval required when used in a way suggesting a public entity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain a written statement of reasons from the LBR/RCS registrar. A formal reconsideration request may be filed with the same registrar within 15 days. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant may petition the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial section) for an order directing registration, with service on the Public Prosecutor's Office and the RCS. Where the rejection is due to a sensitive token, prior authorization from the competent ministry or CSSF/CAA must be obtained before judicial appeal. The applicant may simultaneously reserve an amended alternative name. The judicial appeal must generally be filed within one month of notification of the final refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office/domiciliation services are permitted in Luxembourg for an SCSp that is a pure holding or treasury vehicle. However, the stated business scope of ISIC 5222 offshore supply vessel leasing is a licensed maritime charter activity requiring real commercial substance. The Luxembourg Maritime Navigation Administration and AML/CFT supervisors expect a physical registered office in Luxembourg, local books and records, a locally reachable general partner or authorized manager, and evidence of day-to-day management being exercised from Luxembourg. A pure virtual-address arrangement is therefore not sufficient or advisable for this entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% (moderate) annual probability of unannounced RCS/Maritime Administration/AML on-site inspection for a licensed offshore marine charter vehicle with proper local substance; likelihood rises to above 70% if a virtual office without substantive local management is used.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and reservation request (online LBR handling fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS/LBR tariff schedule for name reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notary public fees for drafting, consulting and signing the SCSp deed of partnership (statuts/convention de société)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaire in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (tarif des notaires) plus disbursements and VAT (17%)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation filing and publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et des associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS/LBR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS filing and RESA publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RBE administrative filing fee (if applicable; often bundled with RCS)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT due diligence and UBO piercing file: PEP, OFAC, UNSC, EU sanctions and FATF screening of all shareholders and natural persons
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg law firm or approved AML/CFT compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for enhanced due diligence of a medium-risk maritime charter SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization and sworn translations of foreign corporate documents, IDs, powers of attorney and UBO statements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs/Embassies and licensed sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular legalization fees plus market translation rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service for the first year (physical/serviced office, registered address and mail handling)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (EUR 900–1,100 per year plus VAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulatory pre-authorization consultation with Luxembourg Maritime Navigation Administration about offshore supply vessel leasing license
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration de la navigation maritime (ANM), Ministry of Mobility and Public Works

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal opinion on maritime license requirements, tax transparency of SCSp and economic substance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing hourly benchmark (EUR 250–EUR 450 per hour), fixed-fee equivalent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended, notably Articles 103-1 et seq. governing the Société en commandite spéciale (SCSp), together with the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade and companies register, annual accounts and companies' bookkeeping.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), which operates the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 12-14 Erna-Langhorne, L-5630 Mondercange, Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration (demande d'immatriculation) filed with the RCS electronically through the LBR/eJustice portal, accompanied by the duly signed partnership agreement (contrat de société) or its notarial form where adopted.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement and no escrow account obligation for an SCSp. Partnership contributions, whether in cash or in kind, are determined in the partnership agreement and become due in accordance with the contribution schedule, subject to standard AML/KYC verification of the source of funds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a duly convened meeting of the general partner of [●] SCSp, held in Luxembourg on [date], the following resolutions were adopted, effective upon RCS registration: 1. Subscription and Contributions. The partnership interests set out in Schedule A are approved and shall be issued to the limited partners against the contributions stated therein. 2. Registered Office. The registered office is established at [street address], L-XXXX Luxembourg. 3. Officers. [Name] is appointed manager (gérant), and [Name] is appointed deputy manager, with authority to represent the SCSp within the mandate set by the partnership agreement. 4. Administration. The officers are authorised to open bank accounts, retain professional advisers, apply for maritime and operating licences, and complete all RCS, tax, VAT and social security filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name clearance and AML/KYC preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online name search; professional adviser or notary for AML/KYC preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search in the RCS database and confirm that the proposed name containing the suffix 'SCSp' is distinct and does not contravene Luxembourg public order. Concurrently assemble the AML/KYC file for all partners, including beneficial ownership declarations and source-of-funds evidence, in accordance with the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and suffix request
RCS name search confirmation or reservation request
Identity and address evidence for all general and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, the applicant may amend the proposed name and resubmit. If AML documentation is incomplete, the formation is paused and the deficiencies are cured by supplementary declarations or revised partner identification data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of partnership agreement and capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The partners and, where notarisation is chosen, a Luxembourg notary; notarisation is not mandatory for a private SCSp unless required by ancillary formalities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the partnership agreement (contrat de société) containing the identity of the general and limited partners, contributions, profit and loss apportionment, management powers and decision-making rules. Execute the agreement by all partners either by private deed or notarial deed, then record the subscribed contributions in Schedule A. No statutory paid-in capital or escrow account is required.
required_dossiers: Schedule of contributions and subscription commitments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner fails to execute or a contribution is queried, the parties may execute a supplementary deed, revise the contribution schedule, or adjust the partnership agreement before filing with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and central business register enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), acting through the electronic eJustice/LBR filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic registration application with the RCS, attaching the executed partnership agreement and the required supporting dossiers. Pay the applicable filing fee. After verification of the legal form, name and submitted instruments, the RCS issues the registration number and the Central Business Register identification number for the SCSp.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement or notarial copy
Power of attorney for the filing representative, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Within the RCS query period, respond to any clarification request or file a corrected rectification. If the application is rejected because of legal form or name, amend the partnership agreement and resubmit the registration request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR arranges publication of the SCSp's registration particulars and relevant instruments in RESA. Verify that the published extract accurately reflects the company name, RCS number, registered office, liability regime and officers. Any subsequent amendment to the partnership agreement must be filed and published separately.
required_dossiers: Officer and partner details for publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If incorrect publication is identified, submit a correction request through the LBR/eJustice portal and provide the RCS certificate showing the correct particulars. Retain proof of submission for third-party reliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security and beneficial-ownership filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for value-added tax and, where relevant, direct tax filings with AEDT. If staff are engaged, register with CCSS as an employer. File the beneficial ownership declaration with the RCS. For offshore marine charter operations, obtain an EORI number where customs or intra-Community movement formalities will apply.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate and CBE identification number
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
VAT and corporate tax registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or social security authority queries the application, submit the requested clarification through MyGuichet or the respective administration portal. Correct any mismatched identification details and re-enroll if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Maritime Administration (Administration de la navigation) under the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the authorisation to operate or charter offshore platform support vessels, and provide technical, insurance, safety and environmental compliance documentation. If vessels are to be registered under the Luxembourg flag, file the vessel registration application and obtain the ship's certificate. Ensure ISM, ISPS, MARPOL and classification society certification is in place for any crewed vessel.
required_dossiers: Offshore support vessel chartering licence application
Vessel registration or bareboat charter documentation
MARPOL and classification society compliance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Maritime Administration requires additional safety, insurance or environmental data, respond with a technical compliance dossier and, if necessary, arrange remedial certification through a recognised classification society or a qualified safety consultant.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Mobility and Public Works – Luxembourg Maritime Administration (Administration de la navigation)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Luxembourg Offshore Support Vessel Chartering and Operation Authorisation (Autorisation d'exploitation de navires de service offshore)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Environment Protection Agency of Luxembourg (Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D – exemption or simplified environmental registration for pure chartering and leasing activities with no onshore installation; a pre-notification environmental compliance statement is required if a shore base or depot is used; full EIA applies only where a shore installation or port facility meets the Annex I thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Operational oily-water discharges under MARPOL Annex I must pass through an oily-water separator calibrated to 15 ppm and meet the applicable en-route distance requirements; untreated sewage discharge is prohibited within 3 nautical miles and must satisfy MARPOL Annex IV treatment standards; MARPOL Annex VI imposes a global fuel sulphur cap of 0.50% m/m and 0.10% m/m inside Emission Control Areas; VOC and cargo vapour emissions must be controlled in approved loading facilities; waste handling must follow MARPOL Annex V, with a prohibition on plastics discharge and documented ship-recycling waste records under EU Regulation 1257/2013.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours for the registered office and any onshore premises; occupational health clearance and structural load verification by the Inspection du travail et des mines for any shore base or workshop; for crewed vessels, valid ISM Safety Management Certificate, flag-state safety certificates and applicable ISPS security clearance must be maintained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from CGDIS for the Luxembourg registered office and any physical premises; ITM workplace suitability and structural load inspection for shore bases and offices; vessel-side compliance includes ISM certification, Safety Management Certificate, flag-state inspections and maritime labour requirements where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — direct tax; Administration des Douanes et Accises — customs; digital portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu) / Guichet.lu (https://guichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or Luxembourg SCSp engaged in taxable supplies must file the Luxembourg VAT registration application with the AEDT, either electronically through MyGuichet.lu or on paper with a signed power of attorney. The authority issues a VAT identification number in the format 'LU' plus 8 digits. A tax representative may be required for non-EU established persons without a fixed establishment; the SCSp is registered in its own name when it acts as a VAT taxable person. Registration should be obtained before performing the first taxable supply; the same VAT number is used for intra-community transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Luxembourg domestic law; a Luxembourg SCSp is mandatorily tax transparent. No US-style check-the-box election exists. ATAD hybrid mismatch rules may recharacterize the vehicle or the participating partner in cross-border structures; an advance tax ruling can confirm tax qualification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident small-business exemption: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover; for non-residents and organized offshore chartering, registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg (no monetary threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping is mandated for B2B invoices. E-invoicing is accepted if authenticity, integrity and legibility are preserved; B2G e-invoicing via Peppol is mandatory for the central administration and public-contractor supplies. Invoices must be retained in original form for 10 years and be transparent to VAT audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to territories outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT where the supplier proves physical removal from the EU within the prescribed period and retains supporting documents. Offshore vessel chartering/leasing supplied to a business customer established outside Luxembourg is outside Luxembourg VAT scope under the B2B place-of-supply rule; where the vessel is leased for voyage/offshore international supply outside EU territorial waters, an export/zero-rate exemption may apply. Long-term charters made available to an EU-established customer inside Luxembourg/EU remain taxable at the standard 17% unless a specific exemption for means of transport used in international navigation is substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic export declaration)
Bill of Lading or equivalent maritime transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT confirmation, or bank payment evidence (proof of proceeds repatriation)
Certificate of Registry or vessel identification evidence
Proof of dispatch/export (port authority or carrier evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities (AEDT) apply strict export substantiation rules: if the exported/chartered vessel transaction lacks the chain of customs, transport, voyage and payment documentation, the 0% rate is denied and the invoice becomes subject to Luxembourg VAT at 17%, with statutory late interest and penalties. Repeated or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger administrative fines, retroactive clawback for the limitation period (generally three years, extended to ten years in fraud cases), possible criminal sanctions and the blacklisting of the exporter as a 'missing trader/fake exporter'; all offshore charter invoices and foreign-exchange remittances are therefore scrutinized as an integrated audit trail.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the euro-area National Central Bank and monetary authority; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the prudential, conduct and AML/CFT supervisor for all credit institutions and payment services in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the EU fully liberalised capital and payments regime under TFEU Articles 63-66 and Directive 88/361/EEC. The euro is fully convertible on current and capital account; there is no separate conversion permit, no BCL exchange-control approval, and no restriction on invoicing, settlement or profit remittance for a Luxembourg SCSp. The SCSp may freely hold USD and other currency operating accounts in Luxembourg or abroad. Practical profit-remittance friction is limited to: (i) EU/UN/OFAC financial sanctions screening; (ii) the bank's internal shipping-sector enhanced due diligence; and (iii) BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations. The CSSF, not the BCL, imposes documentation obligations for the opening of accounts by partnerships without legal personality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline applies to charter hire, freight or any trade receivable received in EUR or foreign currency by the SCSp. Receipts may be retained in the invoicing currency, converted at market rates, or cleared via non-Luxembourg rails. The only mandatory requirement is statistical: cross-border receipts and payments must be declared by the reporting credit institution under the BCL balance-of-payments framework; ultimate-partner-level data must be available on demand. For outbound dividends or withdrawals from an SCSp, Luxembourg applies no withholding tax at partnership level; the partners' tax residence and the transparent classification govern any investor-level taxation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail. Legal constraints: a Luxembourg or European Electronic Money Institution (EMI) regulated under PSD2 cannot provide commercial lending, commercial letters of credit, ship-mortgage escrow, TARGET2 direct participation or full trade-finance documentation; EMIs also typically terminate onboarding for medium-risk maritime chartering entities due to enhanced due diligence requirements and correspondent-bank de-risking. Feasible only as an auxiliary disbursement channel for low-value crew payments and general OPEX, to a maximum monthly threshold, and strictly disclaimed for vessel acquisition, charter-hire receipts or escrow balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A fully remote account opening is generally not permitted for a non-regulated, non-resident-owned SCSp in the offshore chartering sector. In standard practice the Luxembourg bank mandates a physical onboarding interview attended by the SCSp's gérant (general partner) or its duly authorised Luxembourg corporate representative, each individual or entity UBO with 25% or more of capital, and the statutory directors of the corporate GP. The amended Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004, together with CSSF guidance, allows video-based e-KYC and EBA/GL/2022/15-compliant authentication only where a pre-existing group relationship exists; a first-time Luxembourg entry by an offshore vessel-leasing SCSp is treated as a high-intensity face-to-face case.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: SCSp is a partnership without separate legal personality; ambiguity regarding who owns the bank account and which party may pledge or expose funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership deed (contrat de société) together with the contractual segregation declaration (acte de contractualité); RCS extract evidencing registration of the SCSp under the Law of 12 July 2013; copy of the Law of 23 March 2018 (comptes et paiements) acknowledgement permitting accounts in the SCSp name; management clause designating the gérant; written account mandate executed by the gérant; resolution of the special partner(s) approving the onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: offshore supply vessel chartering flagged as maritime-enhanced risk; insufficient provenance of vessel purchase monies and potential sanctions-evasion exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bill of sale and invoice for each vessel; vessel registry and flag-state certificate; class society certificates (ISM/ISPS); P&I and H&M insurance policies; executed time-charter and bareboat-charter documentation; three-year fleet operating plan; bank-stamped source-of-funds statements for all capital contributions; sanctions compliance certificate confirming no operations in EU/OFAC-restricted waters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opaque pass-through ownership chain with multiple intermediate SPVs; inability to map economic substance to ultimate owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) certificate of the SCSp and of every intermediate holding entity; CSSF AML Form No. 1 (client admission and mandate) with complete AML annex; organisational chart certified by legal counsel; tax residence certificates and, where applicable, Luxembourg income-tax ruling (aaccord préalable) confirming pass-through classification; corporate extracts dated within three months and apostilled where relevant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: trade-route opacity and exposure of the chartered platform support vessel to secondary sanctions enforcement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter-party clauses imposing compliance with EU Regulation 2019/1880, UN restrictive measures and OFAC sanctions; voyage and geographical operating-rider declaration; confirmation that no Russian, Iranian, Syrian or Cuban counterparty is involved; enhanced screening results on all counterparties; LMAA or SIM arbitration clause and governing law confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from partners are routed in EUR via TARGET2 using the SCSp IBAN/BIC at a Luxembourg bank, or in USD via SWIFT MT103 to a USD nostro account maintained by the Luxembourg bank outside the eurozone. Each payment is tagged with the Eurosystem balance-of-payments statistic purpose code for cross-border direct investment equity capital or shareholder loan, as applicable, subject to the bank's declaration duty to the BCL. Required verification: capital account ledger of the SCSp, notarised capital commitment clauses in the partnership deed, and source-of-funds evidence from the remitting partner; no BCL prior authorisation is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of vessel acquisition, dry-docking, bunkering, crew, insurance and other marine trade obligations is executed through the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for standard operational wire transfers and charter-hire pass-through; (2) SWIFT MT202/202COV for interbank euro liquidity bridging in correspondent chains; (3) commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 and eUCP version 2.0 for major CAPEX and shipyard payments; (4) documentary collections under URC 522 for freight-related title documents; and (5) a dedicated escrow-maritime facility, operated by a tier-one Luxembourg bank or a regulated trustee, holding deposits and disbursing the purchase price against deliverable memorandum-of-agreement milestones of the vessel sale contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright forward (vanilla FX forward, fixed date or vanilla window)
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX swap (rollover of spot against forward, deliverable)
Cross-currency swap between USD-denominated charter-hire receivables and the EUR-denominated debt service of the SCSp funding stack

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on EUR/CNH or other restricted-deliverable currency exposures, permitted only when a real contracted commercial exposure exists, executed with an EU-authorised credit institution, reported under EMIR, and subject to initial and variation margin where the counterparty is not a qualifying central counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements of the SCSp filed with the principal trade register; where the constitutive agreement does not require preparation, a filing exemption declaration is submitted for micro-undertakings that meet the legal small-company thresholds.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), filed electronically through the LBR eJustice portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval by the partners and no later than seven months after balance-sheet date; a calendar-year SCSp must file by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the gérant to a district-court injunction with a daily fine (astreinte) up to EUR 250; after formal notice and consecutive non-filing, the RCS may apply to the court for administrative strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner reconfirmation (RBE annual validation) and filing of any changes in direct or indirect ownership arising from a transfer of partnership interests.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Change-driven declaration within one month of any transfer or change in control; annual reconfirmation no later than 31 July for a 31 December financial year-end when aligned with the accounts approval cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is a criminal offence carrying fines up to EUR 5,000 and imprisonment for the responsible gérant; the LBR may also refuse to issue RCS extracts and certificates until the RBE file is regularised.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg income-tax and net-wealth-tax return of the SCSp, including the allocation schedule to partners for income-tax transparency purposes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Inland Revenue, via the eCDF electronic filing channel.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SCSp, the return is due by 31 December of the following tax year; professional filers may obtain extensions to 30 June or later by agreed annual derogation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file permits the ACD to assess ex officio; a late-filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax (minimum EUR 150) is applied, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
